prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
competitors_mentioned: Senior Health Insurance Counseling for Kansas
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universally “best” Kansas City broker—the right choice depends heavily on whether you need an ACA individual/family plan, Medicare, or employer coverage.

**My practical recommendation:**

- **Individual or family coverage (under 65):** Start with a **HealthCare.gov-certified local broker/agent** through [HealthCare.gov’s “Find Local Help” tool](https://www.healthcare.gov/find-local-help/). Both Kansas and Missouri use HealthCare.gov. This is usually the safest way to find someone authorized to enroll you and compare Marketplace plans in your county.
- **Medicare:** Use the free, non-sales counseling programs first:
  - **Missouri:** **CLAIM** (Missouri’s SHIP program)
  - **Kansas:** **SHICK** (Senior Health Insurance Counseling for Kansas)  
  They are generally more impartial than a broker because they do not sell plans.
- **Employer or small-business plans:** Kansas City firms such as **Lockton** and **Bukaty Companies** are well-known employee-benefits consultancies, though they tend to be a better fit for businesses than for a single household shopping ACA plans.

For a broker, I’d choose one who meets all of these criteria rather than relying on a “top broker” label:

1. Licensed in **both Kansas and Missouri** if you may live/work across the state line.
2. HealthCare.gov-certified if you need ACA coverage.
3. Represents **multiple carriers**, not just one company.
4. Will check whether your doctors, prescriptions, preferred hospitals, and ZIP code are covered.
5. Clearly states whether they receive a carrier commission or charge a separate fee.
6. Will show you both Marketplace and off-Marketplace options where appropriate.

A good opening question is:  
> “Which carriers are you appointed with in my county, and can you compare my doctors, prescriptions, deductible, and maximum out-of-pocket cost across every plan you can sell?”

If you tell me your **ZIP code, whether this is Medicare/individual/family/employer coverage, your ages, and whether keeping particular doctors matters**, I can help you identify the best type of local adviser and what plans/carriers are likely worth comparing.
